analysis.one_liner: BPCL is a government-controlled company that imports and refines crude oil and sells petrol, diesel and LPG through its retail network across India.
analysis.whats_happening: BPCL's board meets on 23 October 2026 — about a week from now — to approve Q2 FY27 (July-September 2026) results. The prior quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) was a standalone net loss of roughly ₹3,962 crore, against a profit of ₹6,124 crore a year earlier, as diesel marketing margins fell to around -₹25/litre and petrol to about -₹7.7/litre while retail prices stayed fixed. Brent crude reportedly spiked toward $120/bbl late in the September quarter, which is the main swing factor to watch in the upcoming print.
analysis.plain_terms: BPCL doesn't freely set the price it charges at the pump — that is effectively a policy decision — so its quarterly profit depends heavily on the gap between crude costs and retail prices rather than on how well the company runs its refineries or sells fuel. That gap briefly went deeply negative in the June 2026 quarter and turned a year-ago profit into a loss; it is not yet clear from available data whether it has recovered since. This makes the stock look cheap on a trailing P/E of about 8x, but the 'cheapness' partly reflects that the earnings number itself is the volatile, policy-dependent part of the story, not a sign of steady business growth.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026): standalone net loss of ~₹3,962 crore vs. a profit of ₹6,124 crore a year earlier, consolidated loss ~₹1,873 crore vs. profit ₹6,839 crore, even as revenue rose ~23% YoY to roughly ₹1.59 lakh crore. The loss was driven by deeply negative marketing margins (diesel ~-₹25.2/litre, petrol ~-₹7.7/litre), not a refining problem — Bina refinery GRM was a strong $57/bbl and gross GRM for the company was $41.41/bbl, though net GRM after duties was closer to $17/bbl. Q4 FY26 (March 2026) PAT was up 28% YoY to ~₹5,624 crore but down ~22% sequentially from Q3 FY26's ₹7,188 crore. Full FY26 PAT was ₹25,843 crore, up 93.8% YoY from ₹13,337 crore — this jump is very likely a marketing-margin recovery cycle rather than durable operating improvement, so it should not be read as 'growth' in the usual sense. One brokerage (PL Capital) characterised Q1 FY27 as an earnings beat on 'strong refining performance,' which appears to reference adjusted GRM strength rather than the headline reported loss — flagging this as a framing contradiction worth noting rather than resolving.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 24.4% from its 9 February 2026 peak of ₹388.3 to the current ₹293.5, inside a 52-week range of ₹271.3-388.3. This drawdown is not a corporate-action artifact: the last stock split (2-for-1) took effect in June 2024, well before the February 2026 peak, so the price series already reflects it cleanly. Over 3 years the stock has returned 94.3% versus the Nifty's 16.8% and peer IOC's 67.2% — a strong run. But over 5 years the picture flips: BPCL is up 57.2% versus the Nifty's 25.3% and peer IOC's 93.3%, meaning IOC has actually outperformed BPCL over the longer window. So the recent 3-year outperformance is a comeback from a weaker base, not an across-the-board lead over peers.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 8.2x, BPCL looks inexpensive relative to the broader market, but it is actually the most expensive of the three listed state refiners — IOC trades near 5.6x and HPCL near 6.6x. The premium is not unexplained: BPCL's ROE (~26-29%) and ROCE (~25.6%) are meaningfully higher than IOC's (~20% ROE) and HPCL's (~21.6% ROE), largely credited to the Bina refinery's stronger refining economics. So BPCL is 'cheap' only in an absolute, market-wide sense — relative to its own OMC peer group it is priced at a premium for better returns on capital, and whether that premium is justified depends on whether Bina's advantage persists through the current capex-heavy expansion. Debt-to-equity and EV/EBITDA could not be verified from available sources — check on Screener.
analysis.growth_read: This is a margin-led story, not a volume-led one. Refining throughput in Q1 FY27 was 10.15 MMT, and the 23% YoY revenue rise that quarter was driven largely by prices/trading rather than higher volumes. The FY26 profit surge (up 93.8% YoY) reflects a marketing-margin recovery cycle — the gap between crude cost and fixed retail prices widening in BPCL's favour — rather than the business selling meaningfully more fuel or expanding capacity yet. Margin-led swings in a regulated commodity business like this are inherently less durable than genuine volume growth, since they can and have reversed sharply (as in Q1 FY27).
analysis.health_read: In a normal margin environment, OMC profits have historically converted reasonably well into operating cash, but that link breaks down in quarters like Q1 FY27 where the reported loss stems from marketing margins, not asset quality. The bigger watch item is capex: management has guided ₹22,000-25,000 crore of capex for FY27, rising to ₹35,000 crore by FY28-29, with a ₹49,000 crore Bina refinery/petrochemical expansion underway (physical progress ~14% against a ~16% schedule) — debt-to-equity could not be verified, so the funding mix for this capex is Not verified - check on Screener. The dominant risk here is business/regulatory risk (government-influenced pump pricing determining margins), not balance-sheet distress, since there is no pledging (the promoter is the Government of India).
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the Government of India (President of India), holding 52.98% as of the June 2026 quarter, unchanged quarter-on-quarter — pledging is not applicable to a sovereign promoter. FII holding fell sharply from 19.57% to 16.84% over the quarter, while DII holding rose to 21.9% and mutual fund holding rose to 9.56%, suggesting domestic institutions absorbed some of the foreign selling. The Government of Singapore holds about 1.03%. No other marquee individual or marquee fund investor was found on the register — if you were expecting a well-known name here, it is not currently present based on available data.
strengths: ROE of ~26-29% and ROCE of ~25.6% are the highest among the three listed OMCs (IOC ~20% ROE, HPCL ~21.6% ROE)
Bina refinery posted a GRM of $57/bbl in Q1 FY27, well above the company's blended net GRM of ~$17/bbl, underpinning the premium valuation
Dividend yield of ~5.96% (TTM dividend ₹17.5/share) is backed by the DIPAM CPSE policy requiring a minimum payout of 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher
3-year return of 94.3% has meaningfully outpaced both the Nifty (16.8%) and peer IOC (67.2%)
watchpoints: Marketing margins can turn sharply negative within a single quarter — diesel margin was ~-₹25/litre in Q1 FY27 — turning a prior-year profit into a loss purely on the crude-cost/retail-price gap, independent of operating performance
Capex is ramping to ₹22,000-25,000 crore in FY27 and ₹35,000 crore by FY28-29 for the ₹49,000 crore Bina expansion; debt-to-equity to fund this is not verified
FII holding dropped from 19.57% to 16.84% in the latest quarter — worth watching whether this outflow continues
Q2 FY27 results (23 October 2026) land after a reported crude spike toward $120/bbl late in the September quarter, which could squeeze margins again the way it did in Q1 FY27
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due at the 23 October 2026 board meeting — specifically whether diesel and petrol marketing margins recovered from Q1's deeply negative levels — will show whether the June-quarter loss was a one-off cost-price mismatch or a sign that margin pressure is continuing into FY27.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly results cross-checked across PSUConnect, Indian Masterminds, Business Standard, Angel One, Groww and an earnings-call transcript (via Investing.com/Alpha Spread). Valuation metrics from Screener.in/Tickertape; shareholding from Equitymaster/Trendlyne. Not verified - check on Screener: debt-to-equity ratio, EV/EBITDA, exact AGM date, FY27 dividend record date. PE estimates ranged 7.45x-8.22x across sources; used ~8.2x (Screener.in) as primary. One brokerage (PL Capital) described Q1 FY27 as an earnings beat on refining strength despite the headline standalone net loss — likely referencing adjusted/core GRM rather than reported PAT; flagged as a contradiction rather than resolved. The stock's 2024 split (2-for-1) predates the Feb 2026 peak, so the recent 24.4% drawdown is a genuine price move, not a split artifact; no demerger/spin-off was found affecting the current price series (the 2021 Numaligarh Refinery stake sale is unrelated to the current period).
